========================================================================================
TARGET 2 -- Keller Jordan's newtonschulz5 (THEIR bytes, RUN) vs our transcription
========================================================================================
  note: their line 6 is `X = G.bfloat16()`, ours keeps the input dtype.
  bf16 on CPU is 8 mantissa bits, so agreement is only ~1e-2; that is the
  cost of running THEIR shipped configuration, and is reported, not hidden.
  (768, 64)    theirs per-entry=5.4278e-02 | ours(f64) per-entry=5.5038e-02 | max|diff|=6.174e-03  (bf16 floor)
  (64, 768)    theirs per-entry=3.4845e-02 | ours(f64) per-entry=3.4851e-02 | max|diff|=8.266e-03  (bf16 floor)
  (256, 256)   theirs per-entry=2.2118e-02 | ours(f64) per-entry=2.2030e-02 | max|diff|=6.890e-03  (bf16 floor)
  (1000, 32)   theirs per-entry=3.4402e-02 | ours(f64) per-entry=3.5356e-02 | max|diff|=1.115e-02  (bf16 floor)
  eps handling: theirs `X /= (X.norm() + 1e-7)`, ours `.clamp_min(1e-7)`.
  identical for any matrix whose Frobenius norm exceeds 1e-7; they differ
  only on a matrix small enough that the norm itself is below the floor.
    ||G||_F = 6.377e-08 -> theirs denom 1.637737e-07, ours denom 1.000000e-07

========================================================================================
  (768, 64)    rank64    sig_max: ours=33.383836801  LAPACK=35.994674478  rel=7.25e-02   retraction vs LAPACK polar, rel F = 7.8242e-08  sig_max(out)=1.000000000
  (64, 768)    rank64    sig_max: ours=34.794356831  LAPACK=35.140901692  rel=9.86e-03   retraction vs LAPACK polar, rel F = 4.2654e-07  sig_max(out)=1.000000000
  (256, 256)   rank256   sig_max: ours=30.578788363  LAPACK=32.024784409  rel=4.52e-02   retraction vs LAPACK polar, rel F = 2.7029e-01  sig_max(out)=1.000000000
  (4096, 64)   rank64    sig_max: ours=67.910292998  LAPACK=71.601684952  rel=5.16e-02   retraction vs LAPACK polar, rel F = 3.1760e-15  sig_max(out)=1.000000000
  (512, 128)   rank128   sig_max: ours=32.380505685  LAPACK=33.417475553  rel=3.10e-02   retraction vs LAPACK polar, rel F = 5.0907e-04  sig_max(out)=1.000000000
  (768, 64)    rank32    sig_max: ours=33.260411509  LAPACK=35.801870834  rel=7.10e-02   retraction vs LAPACK polar, rel F = 8.2043e-08  sig_max(out)=1.000000000

  the reference for the retraction is therefore NOT absent: it is
  polar(X) = U V^T from LAPACK, i.e. the DEFINITION, and the question the
  iteration answers is 'how close did we get to it'. What has no external
  reference is the CHOICE of coefficients, iteration count and prescale --
  those are design decisions, and no oracle can adjudicate them.
